title: Evidence & proof Activity drawer is permanently empty and the events counter is stuck at 0 (session, proof, and replay)
reproducibility: Always (session mid-flow, final proof page, and replay mode; all tabs Activity+Verifier empty, Provenance populated)
journey: Learner completes (or replays) the fair test and opens the Evidence & proof drawer to inspect the event chain
prerequisites: Any active or completed session, or open /replay/leakage-01
steps: Start 'Try verified sample' and progress to step 4 (or complete the loop to /proof/<id>, or open /replay/leakage-01).
Observe the bottom bar reads '0 events'.
Click '0 events Open' to open the Evidence & proof drawer.
Read the Activity tab (and Verifier tab).
In parallel, GET /api/sessions/<id>/events and count the server-side events.
expected: The Activity feed lists the hash-chained session events (session.created, belief_test.proposed/confirmed, prediction.committed, lab.verified, experiment.completed, transfer.passed, patch.verified, reasoning_diff.issued) and the counter reflects the real count (13 for a completed session).
actual: Counter shows '0 events' at every stage; Activity tab says 'No activity evidence yet. It will appear here when the session produces it.' even on the final proof page; Verifier tab likewise empty. Only the Provenance tab shows data (artifact/session/result hashes). Server API /api/sessions/<id>/events returns all 13 events.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Mid-session at step 4, drawer Activity tab empty + '0 events' while server held 7 events.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: On final /proof page after completion, Activity tab still 'No activity evidence yet', counter still 0; Verifier tab also empty; Provenance tab populated.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Replay mode (/replay/leakage-01) drawer also shows 'No activity evidence yet' + '0 events' despite the replay's 'Stored evidence chain' claim.

evidence.label: Observed in network response
evidence.detail: GET /api/sessions/session_f0a81fbb-.../events returned 13 hash-chained events with timestamps 04:41:05-04:53:01Z.

likely_cause: Client-side event feed is never populated (failed/absent fetch or subscription for the drawer; the counter reads the same empty client list). Provenance is rendered from session aggregate data, which is why only that tab works.
unverified: Whether the drawer populates in the live (non-sample) mode, which I could not test (file upload unavailable).
learner_impact: A learner who opens 'Evidence & proof' to see the promised transparent event chain sees nothing, undermining the core 'prove it like science' lesson.
judge_impact: A judge evaluating the differentiating evidence-transparency feature finds it non-functional in every mode they try; looks broken in the demo.
trust_impact: High - the product's central promise is visible evidence; an empty feed plus a wrong 0 counter reads as either broken or theatrical.
recommended_correction: Wire the drawer Activity/Verifier tabs to GET /api/sessions/<id>/events (already available and hash-chained) and render sequence, actor, kind, and timestamp; make the counter reflect the fetched count; populate equivalent recorded events in replay mode.
smallest_correction: If the feed cannot be shipped, hide the 'N events' counter and the empty Activity/Verifier tabs and keep only the working Provenance tab, rather than display a false 0.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the drawer on any session or replay shows the real event list with count matching /api/sessions/<id>/events; counter equals the number of events at every step.
regression_test: Complete a sample session; assert the drawer Activity tab lists >=12 events and the counter equals GET /api/sessions/<id>/events length; repeat on /replay/leakage-01.
effort: Small-Medium (frontend wiring to an existing endpoint).
score_leverage: High (Design + Technological Implementation: makes the flagship evidence feature actually work).

title: Bogus /replay/<id> lands on a perpetual 'Opening this replay...' spinner after the not-found toast
journey: User follows or mistypes a replay link
steps: Visit https://counterlab.cserules.workers.dev/replay/bogus-id-xyz.
Observe the toast and the main panel.
Wait; observe the page never resolves.
expected: A terminal not-found state: clear message, no spinner, and a recovery CTA (e.g. 'Open the verified replay' or 'Back to home').
actual: Toast 'Replay bogus-id-xyz was not found' appears, but the main panel stays in a perpetual 'CHECKING STORED EVIDENCE / Opening this replay...' loading state that never resolves; the wizard header misleadingly shows step 3 'Test' with Question and Prediction ticked; the only recovery is 'Start over'.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Toast plus indefinite spinner, URL unchanged, misleading step-3 progress chrome.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Agent 1 independently recorded the same 'Replay <id> was not found' + perpetual spinner.

likely_cause: The replay loader has no terminal error branch: after the fetch rejects, the toast fires but the loading state is never cleared and the route never redirects.
unverified: Whether the spinner ever times out (observed for several minutes; never resolved).
learner_impact: A learner with a bad link is stuck on a fake loading screen with false progress and no explanation of what to do next.
judge_impact: A judge probing robustness hits an amateur indefinite-spinner dead end on a flagship route.
trust_impact: High - indefinite loading after a visible error signals fragile state handling.
recommended_correction: On replay fetch failure, render a terminal error panel (message + 'Watch the verified replay' and 'Back to home' CTAs) and reset the wizard chrome to a neutral state.
smallest_correction: Stop the spinner and show static 'Replay not found' text with a home link.
acceptance_criteria: Visiting /replay/<unknown> shows a stable not-found page within one load cycle, with no spinner and at least one working recovery CTA; header shows no fake step progress.
regression_test: Visit /replay/does-not-exist; assert no loading indicator remains after load settles and a recovery CTA is present.
score_leverage: Medium-High (Design: removes a visible dead end on a judge-facing route).

title: Entire session and replay API is unauthenticated - full learner data and signed proof bundle readable by any URL holder; sessions persist >=6h
journey: Anyone who obtains a session URL (shared link, screenshot, referrer, log) reads the full session
user: Learner (whose data is exposed); teacher/judge (assessing data handling)
steps: Complete a session and note its id.
From any unauthenticated context, GET /api/sessions/<id> and /api/sessions/<id>/events.
Observe the full response.
Revisit a 6+ hour-old completed session's /proof/<id> and downloads.
expected: A documented, deliberate exposure model: e.g. short-lived or revocable share links, session TTL/expiry, or at minimum an explicit 'anyone with the link can view' notice and robots/noindex.
actual: GET /api/sessions/<id> returns the complete session with no authentication: the learner's free-text claim, their written revision, the sealed prediction with confidence, the full notebook patch diff, and the entire HMAC-signed proof bundle including its signature. A session completed 6.2 hours earlier was still fully readable and its downloads still worked. No expiry, no auth challenge, no robots.txt.

evidence.label: Observed in network response
evidence.detail: GET /api/sessions/session_4301ab06-... returned ~34KB JSON with beliefTest, prediction, patchResult.diff, proofBundle.events and integrity.signature, unauthenticated.

evidence.label: Observed in network response
evidence.detail: GET /api/sessions/<id>/events returned the full hash-chained event log, unauthenticated.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Completed session session_4301ab06 (created 2026-07-18T22:15Z) still fully accessible at /proof/<id> with working downloads at 2026-07-19T04:27Z (6.2h).

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: GET /api/replays/leakage-01 returns the full replay payload unauthenticated.

likely_cause: No authN/Z layer on read endpoints (demo scope); session ids are the only capability; no TTL/lifecycle job on the session store.
unverified: Whether session ids are truly unguessable at scale (uuidv4 suggests yes); whether ids leak via referrers/analytics; whether any expiry exists beyond the observed 6.2h window.
learner_impact: A learner's written reasoning and predictions are world-readable to anyone who gets the link; for an education product used by minors this is a serious data-handling gap.
judge_impact: Judges (esp. the VP of Education) may view unauthenticated persistence of learner writing as a maturity/compliance gap for an education tool.
trust_impact: High - conflicts with the product's careful-evidence posture if learner data is silently persistent and public-by-link.
recommended_correction: Add an explicit sharing model: expiring signed share links for proof pages, a session TTL with clear messaging, and a visible privacy note; add robots.txt/noindex; consider redacting free-text learner fields from the public read model.
smallest_correction: Add a clear 'Anyone with this link can view this session' notice on /session and /proof, plus a session expiry (e.g. 24h) and robots.txt disallowing /session and /proof.
acceptance_criteria: A documented TTL or revocation exists; expired/unauthorized reads return 401/404; UI discloses link-based visibility; /api/sessions/<id> for an expired session no longer returns learner free text.
regression_test: Create a session, attempt unauthenticated read after the TTL (or after revocation), assert 401/404; assert robots.txt exists and disallows session/proof paths.
dependencies: Storage lifecycle support (Workers KV/D1 TTL) if expiry is implemented.
score_leverage: Medium (protects Potential Impact credibility for the education audience; avoids a judge downgrade on data handling).

title: Sample/replay 'fixed kernel' results are replayed stored evidence, not live computation - tension with 'Fixed kernel computes every number'
reproducibility: Always (every sample session and the replay)
journey: Learner/judge runs the sample fair test believing the kernel computed it live
prerequisites: Run a sample session or read /api/replays/leakage-01
steps: Run the sample fair test and note the result hash.
Compare with the recorded replay and prior sessions' proof bundles.
Read the lab.verified event payload and versions block.
expected: Either the kernel genuinely computes per session, or the UI/marketing consistently states that sample and replay results are recorded verified evidence.
actual: The experiment result is byte-identical across every observed session (resultHash a6ae7652e04e...; accuracy 0.9847/0.5944/0.6736) and the lab.verified payload states source 'stored-approved-leakage-v1', recordedAt 2026-07-14T11:18:03Z, image 'counterlab-runner:local'. The versions block states environment 'Cloudflare Worker with recorded local Docker runner evidence'. Yet the four-authorities copy says 'Fixed kernel - Computes every number - Runs registered split, metric ... deterministically from versioned inputs', and step 3 says 'Result authority: Fixed kernel'. The replay banner does disclose 'It is not a live model run', but the sample session and /judge do not make the recorded nature as clear.

evidence.label: Observed in network response
evidence.detail: lab.verified payload: source 'stored-approved-leakage-v1', recordedAt 2026-07-14, image counterlab-runner:local; identical resultHash across my session and three prior agents' bundles.

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: versions.environment = 'Cloudflare Worker with recorded local Docker runner evidence'.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Judge page authority C copy 'Fixed kernel - Computes every number'; replay banner 'This path reconstructs recorded events and computed payloads. It is not a live model run.'

likely_cause: Workers cannot run the Docker sandbox, so sample/replay serve the pre-verified recorded result for determinism and cost; marketing copy was written around the architecture rather than the deployment reality.
unverified: Whether the LIVE path (/new, uploaded notebook) genuinely executes on a live kernel (untestable: file input unavailable); health endpoint reports liveKernel 'configured' only.
learner_impact: A learner may believe a live computation just happened for their specific session when it is a canned result; the pedagogy still works but the claim is slightly overstated.
judge_impact: A technically probing judge who diffes two sessions finds identical hashes and may discount 'working non-trivial implementation' unless the recorded-evidence design is clearly presented as intentional.
trust_impact: Medium-High - the product is otherwise unusually candid; this one gap stands out.
recommended_correction: Label the sample path as 'recorded verified evidence (deterministic replay of the 2026-07-14 verified run)' wherever the four-authorities story appears, and state plainly which modes compute live.
smallest_correction: Add one line on step 3 of the sample ('Result authority: Fixed kernel - recorded verified run, replayed deterministically') and a matching footnote on /judge.
acceptance_criteria: A user can tell, without reading the API, that sample/replay results are recorded; live vs recorded modes are explicitly distinguished in the UI.
regression_test: Run two sample sessions; if hashes are identical, assert the UI discloses recorded provenance on the result screen.
score_leverage: Medium (protects Technological Implementation credibility under probing).

title: /new readiness checks render pre-passed instantly with no observable verification
journey: User enters Live mode and is told the environment was checked
steps: Visit /new directly (fresh).
Observe the readiness panel immediately on first paint.
expected: A visible pending state followed by a verified pass/fail (e.g. a probe of /api/health), or copy that does not imply a live check.
actual: On first load, both 'Notebook lesson tools are ready to try' and 'Hosted notebook runner is ready' are already displayed with no pending/spinner state and no observable verification; /api/health separately reports the live components only as 'configured' (not 'available').

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: First /new load rendered both readiness lines instantly at the tool floor with no intermediate state.

evidence.label: Observed in network response
evidence.detail: /api/health: sample/replay 'available' but liveGpt/liveCodex/liveKernel/sandbox only 'configured'.

likely_cause: The readiness panel is static/optimistic copy rather than the result of a real probe, or the probe result is hard-coded to pass.
unverified: Whether a background probe fires after first paint (no state change observed); whether the live path then actually works (upload untestable).
learner_impact: A learner is told the device/runner was checked and is ready when nothing was verifiably checked; failure later would be confusing.
judge_impact: A judge may read the 'readiness checks' as theatre if the live path then cannot be exercised.
recommended_correction: Run real probes (e.g. against /api/health components) with pending/pass/fail states, and surface 'configured vs available' honestly.
smallest_correction: Change copy to 'Live mode is configured for this deployment' instead of implying a completed device check.
acceptance_criteria: The panel shows a pending state and resolves to a real probe result; a failed dependency shows a visible failure with guidance.
regression_test: Block or stub the health probe; assert the panel shows failure rather than a pre-passed message.

title: No real 404 for bad deep links: /session/<bogus> and /proof/<bogus> render home UI under the wrong URL
journey: User opens a mistyped or stale session/proof link
steps: Visit /session/bogus-session-id and /proof/bogus-proof-id.
Observe URL, toast, and page content.
expected: A real not-found page (or a redirect to / with the error carried visibly), so the URL, content, and any status agree.
actual: The URL stays on the bogus path while the app renders the full home UI plus a 'Session not found: <id>' toast. Refreshing or sharing the URL repeats the same mismatch; there is no 404 page anywhere (unknown paths silently redirect to /).

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Bogus /session and /proof each render home UI + not-found toast, URL unchanged.

evidence.label: Reproduced
evidence.detail: Agent 1: no 404 page anywhere; unknown routes silently redirect to /.

likely_cause: SPA catch-all routing with client-side toast rather than a routed not-found view; the Worker serves the app shell for all non-/api paths.
unverified: The HTTP status returned for bogus SPA routes (likely 200 with client handling; exact status not observable).
learner_impact: Confusing: the address bar says one thing, the page says another; nothing stable to bookmark or share for an error.
recommended_correction: Add a routed not-found view (with recovery CTAs) for /session//proof//replay misses, or redirect to / with the error persisted in state.
smallest_correction: After the toast, redirect the URL to / so location and content agree.
acceptance_criteria: Bad deep links resolve to a stable not-found or home URL whose content matches the address bar.
regression_test: Visit /session/nope; assert final URL and rendered view agree and a recovery CTA exists.

title: Missing production basics: no robots.txt, no sitemap.xml; /favicon.ico request timed out once
user: Search engines, browsers, judges inspecting polish
steps: Visit /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /favicon.ico.
expected: robots.txt served (even if minimal); favicon served; sitemap optional but sensible for the public pages.
actual: /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml are swallowed by the SPA fallback and redirect to /. /favicon.ico caused a browser-tool visit timeout on a single attempt (may be tool download-handling rather than a server fault).

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Both /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml rendered the home page (client redirect to /).

evidence.label: Unverified
evidence.detail: Single /favicon.ico attempt timed out in the browser tool.

likely_cause: Static asset routes not handled before the SPA catch-all.
unverified: Whether favicon genuinely 404s/hangs server-side vs tool behaviour.
recommended_correction: Serve /robots.txt (disallow /session and /proof at minimum - see A9-03) and /favicon.ico; optionally /sitemap.xml for /, /judge, /replay/leakage-01.
smallest_correction: Add a two-line robots.txt route in the Worker.
acceptance_criteria: GET /robots.txt returns text/plain directives; favicon returns an icon; neither SPA-redirects.

title: 'Reproduce locally' scripts reference a repository that is not shipped with the deployed demo
journey: Judge attempts to run the reproduce commands from the demo
steps: Scroll to 'Reproduce locally'.
Attempt to obtain ./scripts/test-all.sh etc. from the deployment.
expected: The commands are runnable from artifacts the judge can actually access (repo link, downloadable bundle), or the section states where the repo lives.
actual: Four commands are listed (./scripts/test-all.sh, ./scripts/run-mutations.sh leakage, ./scripts/reproduce-session.sh leakage-01, ./scripts/replay-patch.sh leakage-01) but no repository or script download is reachable from the site; the demo alone cannot reproduce anything.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Reproduce-locally section lists ./scripts/... with no link or bundle.

likely_cause: The Devpost submission likely links the repo, but the deployed dossier was written assuming repo context.
unverified: Whether the Devpost page supplies the repo (outside this black-box scope).
judge_impact: A judge who values the reproducibility story hits a dead end unless the repo is linked on Devpost.
recommended_correction: Link the repository next to the commands, or ship a downloadable reproduce bundle from /judge.
smallest_correction: Add a repo URL line above the command list.
acceptance_criteria: A judge can reach the scripts from the /judge page in one click.
regression_test: Assert the /judge reproduce section contains a reachable link to the scripts.

title: 'Start over' abandons the flow instantly with no confirmation and no in-app way back to the persisted session
journey: User clicks Start over (possibly accidentally) mid-flow or on the proof page
steps: Progress into a session.
Click 'Start over'.
expected: A confirmation for destructive abandonment, and/or a visible way to return to the existing session (the server keeps it).
actual: Clicking 'Start over' immediately navigates to / with no confirmation. The session still exists server-side (proof URL remains valid), but the app offers no link back to it; a user who clicked accidentally loses their place in the UI.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Single click on Start over from the proof page returned to / instantly; session data persisted server-side.

evidence.label: Inferred from behaviour
evidence.detail: Recent sessions appear in the 'Project & evidence' studio drawer per the route map, offering partial recovery, but no direct 'resume' affordance was surfaced at the point of abandonment.

likely_cause: No confirm step on the reset action; recovery relies on the studio drawer rather than an explicit prompt.
unverified: Whether the studio drawer reliably resurfaces this exact session for recovery in all cases.
learner_impact: An accidental click can cost a learner their place (though not their server data).
recommended_correction: Confirm before abandoning ('Start over? Your progress is saved - Resume later or discard'), and surface a Resume link.
smallest_correction: Add a one-step confirm dialog to Start over.
acceptance_criteria: Start over requires confirmation and offers a path back to the existing session.
regression_test: Click Start over, cancel the confirm, assert the session view is unchanged.

title: VERIFIED (positive): the 'belief break in twenty seconds' claim holds (~12.8s kernel run); downloads instant; refresh restores state
reproducibility: Verified once by direct measurement; consistent with 3 prior proof bundles
journey: Learner runs the fair test and later downloads artifacts
steps: Seal a prediction, click 'Run the fair test', and record click time.
Read experiment.completed timestamp from /api/sessions/<id>/events.
Download the proof record and repaired notebook from /proof/<id>.
Refresh mid-wizard and confirm state restore.
expected: The marketed ~20s belief break should be real; artifacts should download without long generation; state should survive refresh.
actual: Kernel run measured at ~12.8s (Run click 04:45:32.2Z to experiment.completed 04:45:45.03Z), inside the 20s claim and the 20s sandbox wallSeconds limit. Plan verify 0.94s, transfer 0.27s, patch verify 1.32s. Proof record (34KB HMAC-signed JSON) and repaired notebook (valid .ipynb with the GroupShuffleSplit patch) both downloaded instantly. Mid-wizard refresh fully restored state; completed /session/<id> redirects to /proof/<id>. Larger end-to-end figures (~10min) are learner reading time, not compute.

evidence.label: Observed in network response
evidence.detail: experiment.completed 04:45:45.025Z vs Run click 04:45:32.2Z = ~12.8s; phase durations from the event log.

evidence.label: Observed in generated artifact
evidence.detail: Downloaded proof bundle parses as signed JSON (12 events, hmac-sha256); downloaded notebook is valid nbformat 4 with the expected patch.

evidence.label: Directly observed
evidence.detail: Refresh at step 4 restored the full wizard state.

likely_cause: Deterministic pre-verified sample path plus server-persisted session state.
unverified: Live-mode (uploaded notebook) performance - untestable in this audit.
learner_impact: The core promise (a ~20s fair test) is honest; the experience is snappy.
judge_impact: The headline performance claim survives direct measurement.
recommended_correction: None for the compute claim; consider clarifying that the full lesson loop takes several minutes of interaction (the 20s is the test itself).
regression_test: Re-run a sample session; assert Run-click to experiment.completed <= 20s.
